title: 11-year-old Carly Rae Jepsen song surges up the charts thanks to GTA VI needle drop
summary: Justin Bieber, Tate McRae, April Wine and other acts are also featured in the game.

image.caption: Carly Rae Jepsen's track Run Away With Me is getting a streaming bump 11 years after its release. (Vanessa Heins)

Justin Bieber, Tate McRae, April Wine and other acts are also featured in the game
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Nov 23, 2026 5:17 PM EST | Last Updated: 3 hours ago
Carly Rae Jepsen's saxophone-backed track Run Away With Me is getting a boost more than a decade after its release, thanks to its inclusion in the blockbuster video game Grand Theft Auto VI.

The song, originally released in 2015, is taking on a new life with a surprise remix in the game: between Nov. 16-22, there was a week over week increase of 157 per cent for listens to Run Away With Me on Spotify.
"Secret's finally out! GTA 6 let's run away together," Jepsen wrote on Instagram.
In a special mission sequence in the game, the song plays while the characters Jason and Lucia ride Sea-Doos.

Jepsen's fans have reacted across social media, with several commenting on YouTube under the music video for the song. "This scene in that mission had me floating bro," wrote @VincentNNS, while @voxious07 wrote, "I love how everyone felt the same feeling at that mission, it was surreal. What a game. What a song. What an experience."
The Weeknd's music also appeared in Vice City, courtesy of French electronic duo Justice.
The Toronto superstar is credited on My Only Vice, an unreleased track featured in the score for the long-awaited video game.

The song is among several original compositions credited to Justice, who created the game's main score. Rockstar Games lists the Weeknd, born Abel Tesfaye, as a co-writer alongside Justice members Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay.
The collaboration follows their work together on Wake Me Up, a track from the Weeknd’s 2025 album Hurry Up Tomorrow.

The Weeknd’s 2013 track Wanderlust is also featured on Flash FM, one of the game's fictional radio stations, alongside fellow Canadian Tate McRae's Sports car and Justin Bieber's 2017 collaboration with BloodPop, Friends.
Toronto rap star Drake also has several tracks in the game, including Nonstop, Nokia and Love Me, his collaboration with Lil Wayne and Future.
His 2013 hit Hold On, We're Going Home, featuring Toronto R&B duo Majid Jordan, is also included.
The official score for GTA VI is set to be released Dec. 11.
Toronto instrumental jazz group BadBadNotGood is featured on Leonida Jazz Radio with Blowin’ Smoke, an apparently unreleased collaboration with American trumpeter Randy Brecker.
Electronic artists also received a boost

Over on Stockyard FM, Vancouver-bred electronic duo Bob Moses appear with their Elderbrook collaboration Inner Light, which gained renewed attention after being featured in a GTA VI trailer earlier this year.
The Grammy-nominated pair, Tom Howie and Jimmy Vallance, told the Canadian Press that the song had racked up more than 50 million new streams since the trailer's release in August.
The duo’s track Nothing But You, remixed by DJ Tennis, is also included in the game, along with Never Come Back by Dundas, Ont.-born electronic artist Caribou.
Montreal metal vets Voivod also get some shine in the game, with their track Panorama featuring on The Chamber 106.6, a heavy music station.
Flip the dial to V-Rock, and you’ll hear Roller by Halifax rock greats April Wine, as well as Loverboy’s ubiquitous ’80s anthem Working for the Weekend.
Montreal-based producer Martyn Bootyspoon is among the musicians credited with contributing to the game's supplemental score.

Music has long been integral to the GTA experience, with the franchise’s fictional radio stations exposing generations of players to an eclectic mix of sounds as they cruise city streets and flee the cops.
Bob Moses said they were paid a relatively modest licensing fee, but the payoff was in the exposure to their music.
“I forget how much money it was, but it’s not enough to remember,” said Howie.
“The opportunity is definitely in the potential for the reach, not in the paycheque.”
